title: Club Membership: proration of the early-termination fee by remaining term
content:
## Scope
This document states how Club Membership prorates the early-termination fee once a member is eligible for it, based on how much of the tier's own minimum committed term remains unelapsed.

## Rule
Once notice of cancellation has been given and the membership is not sitting in past due status, the charge amount is the tier's own listed early-termination fee amount, reduced pro rata by the fraction of the tier's own minimum committed term that remains unelapsed at the moment the charge is assessed. The months elapsed are counted as whole months from the date the membership was opened. The charge is billed only while some whole month of the minimum committed term still remains; a membership that has reached or passed its minimum committed term owes no early-termination fee at all under this basis.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose a tier's own listed early-termination fee is $149.00 and its own minimum committed term is 12 months. For a member with 4 whole months elapsed since the membership was opened, 8 whole months remain, and the pro-rata amount is $149.00 multiplied by the fraction 8 divided by 12, giving approximately $99.33 before any further reduction. For a member with all 12 whole months elapsed, 0 months remain, and no early-termination fee is billed at all.

## Points of judgement
A member with exactly 1 whole month remaining still owes a pro-rata amount under this basis, since some whole month remains; a member with 0 whole months remaining owes nothing under this basis, regardless of how many partial days beyond the minimum term have passed.
